ours-distill.short: Night School's distillation runs, trained for this film
ours-distill.citation: media/school/distill/facts.json, written by tools/school/fill_distill.mjs from system/school/distill.mjs: the attention lesson's model as teacher; a one-floor student of 4,112 numbers trained 2,000 steps on hard labels, the teacher's soft targets at temperatures 1, 2, 4, 8, a half-and-half mix, the teacher's top word, the generator's exact odds, and an untrained teacher; fresh text and fixed pools of 32 and 256 rows; 3 seeds per arm; paired differences called resolved only when every seed agrees in sign and the mean is over two standard errors.
claims: Full data: hard 0.7213, soft T1 0.7019, T2 0.7355, T4 0.7229 (none resolved against hard), T8 0.7612 (worse, resolved).
32-row pool: hard 4.801 at the end (best 1.720), soft T2 1.637 (resolved better); 256-row pool: hard 1.276, soft T2 0.727.
Top word as certain: held-out 3.843, copy accuracy 0.947; untrained teacher 3.839; word counts 3.273.
ours-distill.n: 3 seeds per arm; 256 held-out rows (6,144 targets).
ours-distill.interval: Per-seed values, sd, and paired differences in facts.json.
ours-distill.does_not_prove: Anything about large models; the teacher learned from far more text than the pools, so the low-data result is transfer through the teacher, not learning from 32 rows.

hinton2015.short: Hinton, Vinyals and Dean 2015, Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
hinton2015.citation: Hinton, G., Vinyals, O., Dean, J. (2015). Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network. arXiv:1503.02531 (NIPS 2014 Deep Learning Workshop).
hinton2015.read: to be read by the fact-check
claims: Train a small model on the soft targets of a large one, raising the temperature of the final softmax; the soft-target loss is scaled by T squared to keep gradient magnitudes comparable.
Soft targets let a model trained on very little data (3 percent of the speech training set) keep much of the full model's accuracy.
